name: Curaçao

tax.name: Tax Authority of Curaçao (Inspectie der Belastingen)

legalStatuses.label: Sole trader (registered business)
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.feeNote: The Chamber of Commerce quotes the registration fee. You also need a business licence for your activity.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company (NV or BV) costs more to set up than a sole proprietorship. The Chamber of Commerce quotes the current fees.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
launchSteps.plain: Search the name at the Chamber of Commerce first.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Chamber of Commerce
launchSteps.plain: Every business registers in the commercial register. A company is incorporated through a notary.

launchSteps.label: Apply for your business licence
launchSteps.plain: Most activities need a licence from the government.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Tax Authority (CRIB number)
launchSteps.plain: You get your CRIB number and your turnover tax (OB) account. You file returns even before you have sales.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Social Insurance Bank (SVB)
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people pay old age insurance (AOV) and the general insurance for exceptional medical costs (AVBZ).

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register your employees and prepare payroll payments
launchSteps.plain: With employees you withhold wage tax and pay social insurance premiums every month.

incomeTax.label: Income tax
incomeTax.allowanceNote: basic tax credit of Cg 2,850 a year
incomeTax.bracketText: 9.75% up to Cg 38,225, 15% up to Cg 50,968, 23% up to Cg 76,452, 30% up to Cg 108,306, 37.5% up to Cg 159,273, then 46.5%, minus a basic tax credit of Cg 2,850

contributions.label: Old age insurance (AOV/AWW)
contributions.plain: A pension insurance. Self-employed people pay it on their own income, up to Cg 132,824 a year.

contributions.label: Exceptional medical costs (AVBZ)
contributions.plain: A general insurance for long-term care and exceptional medical costs. It is collected with your income tax return.

vat.label: Turnover tax (OB)
vat.registerNote: A small business scheme (RKO) can exempt very small sole proprietors from filing: ask the Tax Authority.
vat.filingNote: You file annually if your taxable turnover is below Cg 30,000, quarterly up to Cg 75,000, and monthly above that.

calendar.monthlyText: File your turnover tax (OB): annually if your yearly turnover is below Cg 30,000, quarterly up to Cg 75,000 and monthly above that.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: File your income tax return, by April 30.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay wage tax and social insurance premiums for the previous month, by the 15th.
calendar.vatText: File your turnover tax (OB) return for each period, even when you have no sales.

notes: Curaçao has a turnover tax (OB) of 6% on sales, similar to a VAT. Sole proprietors pay income tax on their profit, with a basic tax credit.
Companies pay profit tax at 15% on the first Cg 500,000 and 22% above.
